messages:
Alex Chen: Thinking about per-org rate policy again — proposal: keep RPM/TPM for steady-state billing but add an ephemeral burst-credit allocator that sits at the edge and gives short lived extra concurrency for healthy tenants.
Priya Nair: +1 to separating steady vs burst. question: how do we prevent credit gaming across keys?
Josh Patel: We can tie credits to org-id + region + short nonce window. credits expire in 30s. no cross-region transfer.
Mara Gomez: UX concern: console needs to show 'effective concurrency' not just cap. customers will ask why they still get 429s when they have credits.
Luis Ortega: Enforcement placement: do we enforce at the CDN/edge or at the router? Edge is faster but harder to keep consistent with Dedicated pools.
Alex Chen: Edge enforcement for immediate bursts, router acts as source-of-truth for reconciliation. If router sees mismatch, it will instruct edge to revoke credits.
Priya Nair: Telemetry we need: credits_issued, credits_consume_rate, credits_revoked, percent_429_from_burst. dashboards per-org + aggregate.
Josh Patel: Simulation results I ran on prod-like traces: ephemeral credits reduced tail 429s by ~65% for spiky workloads, cost delta ~ +3%.
Mara Gomez: For console rollout: show timeline + a "burst credits used" chart and a checkbox: "Enable ephemeral bursts (beta)". default off for new enterprise customers.
Katie Wu: Can we have a graceful fallback if credit reconciliation fails? e.g., router keeps a small reserve fallback of 2 concurrency-per-org.
Samir Roy: Yes. fallback reserve helps noisy neighbor cases. also add a per-org debt limit so credits can't go negative past N.
Josh Patel: Policy JSON sketch (edge reads this):
```
{
  "org_id": "<org>",
  "steady_rpm": 1200,
  "steady_tpm": 60000,
  "concurrency_cap": 50,
  "burst_alloc": {
    "window_s": 30,
    "max_additional_concurrency": 20,
    "decay_policy": "linear"
  }
}
```
Priya Nair: Love the simple API. Need to add "max_daily_burst_tokens" to limit sustained bursts.
Alex Chen: Good call. also need admin override in console and an audit log event for every credit grant.
Luis Ortega: Ops runbook for incidents: how to disable bursts globaly and backfill logs. deploy-bot: deployment scheduled to canary tomorrow 09:30 UTC. :robot_face:
deploy-bot: canary rollout started; policy service v2 -> instances in us-west-2 first.
Samir Roy: Migration notes: we should 1) simulate using historical traffic, 2) run canary with 5 orgs, 3) open alpha for low-risk customers, 4) enterprise opt-in.
Mara Gomez: Messaging for customers: "ephemeral burst credits reduce short-lived 429s during legitimate spikes; not intended for sustained heavy usage." Include explainer doc.
Katie Wu: Quick SQL to find orgs that would benefit most (high RPM variance):
```
SELECT org_id, stddev(rpm) as rpm_sd, avg(rpm) as rpm_avg
FROM org_traffic_hourly
WHERE hour >= now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY org_id
ORDER BY rpm_sd desc
LIMIT 50;
```
Josh Patel: Telemetry alert ideas: if credits_revoked_rate > 0.5% for an org => page on-call. Also alert if average burst_consumption > 75% over 10m.
Priya Nair: Privacy/compliance note: keep burst logs minimal — no payloads, just counters and events. tie to KMS for sensitive orgs.
Alex Chen: Next steps: finalize policy JSON with max_daily_burst_tokens, add console toggle + charts, wire metrics, run 48h sim, then canary. I'll draft RFC. Assign owners? Priya (policy + metrics), Josh (sim + infra), Mara (console + docs), Luis (ops/runbook).
Priya Nair: Assigned. i'll start a metrics dashboard board. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Josh Patel: Starting sim job now, will post results here. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Mara Gomez: I'll draft the FAQ and admin copy.
Luis Ortega: I'll update oncall playbook and rollback steps.
Alex Chen: Awesome — aim for canary next week. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
